title: Washington National Guard called up for wildfires
description:
Authorities activated helicopter crews from the Washington National Guard to assist firefighters battling wildfires in Eastern Washington. One UH-60 Blackhawk and one CH-47 Chinook helicopter along with 14 crew and support personnel were sent to the Carlton Complex Fire that is currently burning in the Methow Valley.

Sergeant Cory Churchill, B Co. 1-168 General Support Aviation Battalion,
talks about this being his first wildfire mission and how his training helped him prepare for the real thing.

transcript.text: We have some wildfires going on east, and so they've called us up and activated us to
help support that, drop some water.
We have to get the aircraft prepped ready.
We have to load up our buckets.
Everybody's got to pack at least three or four days worth of stuff because we'll be over
there.
For three, maybe four, it could be five, I don't know.
We'll do a lot of training out around this area.
We do annual fire academics that we have to take online, teach you about fuel sources,
the way fires react, procedures in and around the fire area.
We take buckets out to some of the local lakes around here on the Fort Lewis Reservation
dip in there, and we just do all of our training around here and just get ready for the real
thing.
It's helped me prepare enough, but you never really know how it's going to be until you
actually go out and do it.
I feel confident that I'll do okay, that we'll get the job done.
This is my first fire, yes.
I'm honestly pretty excited about it.
This is actually what I signed up to do in the Guard over seven years ago.
And a lot of people forget that as a National Guard, we're here for them.
We're here to support them and help the state, help them, and support domestic operations,
put out fires, that kind of thing.
It's going to be a lot of hard work.
It's going to be rewarding.
It's going to be a lot of fun.
